title: Unidirectional Data Flow

validation.research: Six primary sources: official Redux concepts/data flow, Elm Architecture, Android UI layer, Redux side effects, Redux Toolkit request-ID examples, and Python frozen dataclasses. The article presents recurring ownership and direction without claiming a sole inventor, one required framework, a compulsory global store, or reducer purity as the universal definition. The current-request and pending guard is explicit application policy, not an inherent cancellation or ordering guarantee.

example_limits: Original sequential in-memory search-state simulation. Search intents create a new screen-local request ID, trim query text to at most 80 Unicode code points, and clear previous results/errors; an empty query invalidates older work without starting retrieval. A pure update accepts matching pending Loaded/Failed completions, ignores stale or duplicate terminal completions, validates IDs and current payload shapes, and returns frozen dataclass state containing immutable values. A pure text view reads the state. The composition owns assignment and manually supplies messages, including an older result arriving last. A real adapter would perform retrieval outside update and dispatch completion to the correct owner. Failed carries a prepared public display message. There is no network adapter, subscription/store framework, task cancellation, screen disposal implementation, cross-process IDs, concurrency synchronization, persistence, authorization, durable action history, or event-sourcing implementation. The settings-form second context is explanatory only.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
